•   **Chapter Introduction:** This chapter, "Know your surroundings," introduces young learners to the immediate environment they live in, helping them understand and appreciate the world around them.
•   **Surroundings Defined:** Our surroundings refer to everything that is present around us, including people, places, animals, plants, and various objects.
•   **Importance of Knowing Surroundings:** Understanding our surroundings helps us navigate our daily lives, identify safe and unsafe places, recognize people who help us, and appreciate the natural world.
•   **Observation Skills:** The chapter encourages children to use their senses – sight, hearing, smell, touch – to observe and learn about the different elements in their environment.
•   **Immediate Environment:** For a Class 1 student, "surroundings" primarily refers to their home, school, neighbourhood, and the common places they visit.
•   **Two Main Categories:** Things in our surroundings can broadly be categorized into two types: natural things and man-made things.
•   **Natural Things:** These are elements that exist in nature without human intervention, such as plants, animals, mountains, rivers, the sun, moon, and stars.
•   **Man-Made Things:** These are objects or structures created by humans, such as houses, roads, cars, toys, and furniture.
•   **Living vs. Non-Living:** Within natural and man-made things, we can also distinguish between living things (that grow, move, breathe, eat) and non-living things (that do not).
•   **Our Home as Surroundings:** The house we live in, with its rooms, furniture, and family members, forms the most immediate part of our surroundings.
•   **Our School as Surroundings:** The school building, classrooms, playground, teachers, and classmates are also a significant part of a child's daily surroundings.
•   **Sensory Exploration:** Children learn to identify different sounds (birds chirping, car horns), smells (flowers, food), and textures (rough tree bark, smooth table) in their surroundings.
•   **Developing Awareness:** The goal is to develop a sense of awareness and curiosity about the environment, fostering a connection with the world outside themselves.
•   **Foundation for EVS:** This chapter lays a fundamental groundwork for understanding broader environmental science concepts in later grades, starting with the familiar.
•   **Personal Connection:** By understanding their surroundings, children begin to see their own place and role within the larger community and environment.

•   **Natural Surroundings: Living Things:** This section focuses on the living components of our natural environment that are not made by humans.
•   **Plants:** Plants are living things that grow from the soil. They come in many shapes and sizes, from tiny grass to tall trees.
•   **Trees:** Trees are large plants with a thick woody stem called a trunk and many branches. Examples include mango trees, neem trees, and banyan trees.
•   **Small Plants:** These include bushes, shrubs, and herbs that are smaller than trees and often have softer stems. Flowers are also part of small plants.
•   **Importance of Plants:** Plants are very important because they give us fresh air to breathe, food to eat (fruits, vegetables), wood for building, and shelter for animals.
•   **Animals:** Animals are living beings that move, eat, and grow. They can be found in various places around us.
•   **Pets:** Some animals live with us in our homes and are called pets, such as dogs, cats, and fish. They are part of our immediate surroundings.
•   **Wild Animals:** Other animals live in forests or jungles and are called wild animals, like lions, tigers, and elephants. We might see them in zoos or books.
•   **Birds:** Birds are animals with feathers, wings, and beaks. They can fly and build nests in trees. Common birds include sparrows, crows, and pigeons.
•   **Insects:** Insects are small creatures with six legs, like butterflies, ants, and mosquitoes. Some insects are helpful (like bees), while others can be harmful.
•   **Interdependence (Simple Concept):** Living things often depend on each other; for example, animals eat plants, and birds build nests in trees.
•   **Caring for Living Things:** We should be kind to animals and plants, not harm them, and help them grow.
•   **Observing Living Things:** Children are encouraged to observe how plants grow, how animals move, and what sounds birds make.
•   **Diversity of Life:** The natural world is full of many different kinds of plants and animals, making our surroundings interesting and beautiful.
•   **Basic Needs of Living Things:** All living things need air, water, and food to survive and grow.

•   **Natural Surroundings: Non-Living Things and Features:** This section explores the non-living components and natural features of our environment.
•   **Sky:** The sky is the vast open space above us. It changes throughout the day and night.
•   **Sun:** The sun is a big star that gives us light and warmth during the day. It helps plants grow and makes our days bright.
•   **Moon:** The moon is a natural satellite that we see in the sky at night. It reflects light from the sun.
•   **Stars:** Stars are tiny, twinkling lights we see in the night sky. They are very far away.
•   **Clouds:** Clouds are made of tiny water droplets or ice crystals floating in the sky. They can bring rain.
•   **Air:** Air is all around us, though we cannot see it. We breathe air to live, and it helps kites fly and windmills turn.
•   **Water:** Water is essential for all living things. We find water in rivers, ponds, lakes, and it comes from rain.
•   **Soil:** Soil is the top layer of the Earth where plants grow. It is home to many small creatures.
•   **Landforms (Basic):** These are natural shapes on the Earth's surface. For Class 1, this might include simple recognition of hills or flat land.
•   **Hills:** Hills are raised areas of land, smaller than mountains. They are natural parts of the landscape.
•   **Rivers:** Rivers are natural flowing bodies of water that move towards a sea or lake.
•   **Ponds/Lakes:** These are natural bodies of still water, smaller than rivers or seas.
•   **Weather:** Weather refers to the condition of the atmosphere at a particular time, including sunshine, rain, wind, and clouds.
•   **Sounds of Nature:** Natural surroundings have distinct sounds, such as the rustling of leaves, the sound of rain, the chirping of birds, or the flowing of water.
•   **Importance of Natural Non-Living Things:** These elements provide the basic resources and conditions necessary for life on Earth, like light, heat, water, and air.

•   **Man-Made Surroundings: Structures:** This section focuses on the buildings and structures created by humans that form a significant part of our environment.
•   **Houses:** Houses are buildings where people live. They provide shelter, safety, and comfort for families.
•   **Different Types of Houses:** Houses can be big or small, made of different materials like bricks, wood, or mud, and can have different shapes.
•   **Purpose of Houses:** Houses protect us from sun, rain, wind, and cold, and keep us safe from dangers.
•   **Schools:** Schools are buildings where children go to learn, study, and play with their friends and teachers.
•   **Shops/Markets:** Shops and markets are places where we can buy things we need, like food, clothes, and toys.
•   **Hospitals/Clinics:** Hospitals and clinics are buildings where doctors and nurses help people who are sick or injured get well.
•   **Roads:** Roads are paths built for vehicles like cars, buses, and bicycles to travel on, connecting different places.
•   **Pavements/Footpaths:** These are special paths next to roads, built for people to walk safely.
•   **Bridges:** Bridges are structures built to cross over rivers, roads, or valleys, making travel easier.
•   **Parks/Playgrounds:** Parks and playgrounds are open areas, often with swings, slides, and open spaces, created for people to relax and children to play.
•   **Streetlights:** Streetlights are lamps placed along roads and paths to provide light at night, making it safer to walk and drive.
•   **Buildings:** The term "buildings" refers to various structures like offices, banks, and community centers, all built by people for different purposes.
•   **Construction Materials:** Man-made structures are built using materials like bricks, cement, wood, glass, and metal.
•   **Human Ingenuity:** These man-made structures demonstrate human creativity and ability to shape the environment to meet their needs.

•   **Man-Made Surroundings: Objects and Transport:** This section covers the various objects and modes of transportation created by humans that are part of our daily surroundings.
•   **Vehicles:** Vehicles are machines designed to transport people or goods from one place to another.
•   **Cars:** Cars are common vehicles used by families for personal travel.
•   **Buses:** Buses are larger vehicles that carry many people together, often on fixed routes.
•   **Bicycles:** Bicycles are two-wheeled vehicles powered by pedaling, used for short distances or recreation.
•   **Trains:** Trains are long vehicles that run on railway tracks, carrying many passengers or heavy goods over long distances.
•   **Aeroplanes:** Aeroplanes are flying vehicles that carry people and goods through the air, allowing for fast travel across long distances.
•   **Toys:** Toys are objects made for children to play with, such as dolls, cars, blocks, and balls, providing entertainment and aiding development.
•   **Furniture:** Furniture includes items like tables, chairs, beds, and cupboards, which are placed in homes and offices for comfort and utility.
•   **Utensils:** Utensils are tools used for cooking, serving, and eating food, such as plates, spoons, and pots.
•   **Clothes:** Clothes are garments worn by people to cover their bodies, protect them from weather, and for fashion.
•   **Tools:** Tools are simple instruments like hammers, screwdrivers, or scissors, used to perform specific tasks.
•   **Machines (Simple Concept):** Machines are devices that make work easier, from simple ones like a bicycle to complex ones like a washing machine.
•   **Electronic Devices:** Common electronic devices like televisions, mobile phones, and computers are also man-made objects in our surroundings.
•   **Importance of Man-Made Objects:** These objects make our lives easier, more comfortable, and allow us to perform various activities efficiently.
•   **Responsible Use:** We should use man-made objects carefully and responsibly, taking care of them so they last longer.

•   **Our Neighbourhood: Places:** This section introduces the concept of a neighbourhood and identifies key places within it that are important for daily life.
•   **Neighbourhood Defined:** A neighbourhood is the area around our home, including the houses, streets, and important places nearby.
•   **School:** The school is a very important place in our neighbourhood where children go to learn, read, write, and play with friends.
•   **Hospital/Clinic:** The hospital or clinic is a place where doctors and nurses work to help people who are sick or injured get better.
•   **Market/Shop:** The market or local shops are places where we can buy groceries, clothes, toys, and other things that our family needs.
•   **Park/Playground:** The park or playground is an open area in the neighbourhood where children can play games, run around, and enjoy fresh air.
•   **Post Office:** The post office is a place where we can send letters and parcels to people in other places, and also receive them.
•   **Police Station:** The police station is where police officers work. They help keep our neighbourhood safe and maintain law and order.
•   **Fire Station:** The fire station is where firefighters work. They help put out fires and rescue people from dangerous situations.
•   **Bank:** A bank is a place where people keep their money safe and can take it out when they need it.
•   **Bus Stop/Railway Station:** These are places where we can catch buses or trains to travel to different parts of the city or other towns.
•   **Library:** A library is a place where we can borrow books to read and learn new things.
•   **Community Helpers at Places:** Each of these places has specific community helpers who work there to serve the neighbourhood.
•   **Familiarity and Safety:** Knowing these places helps children feel familiar with their surroundings and understand where to go for help if needed.
•   **Sense of Community:** Understanding the different places in a neighbourhood helps children develop a sense of belonging to their community.

•   **People in Our Surroundings: Community Helpers:** This section highlights the various people who live and work in our surroundings and help us in different ways.
•   **Family Members:** Our parents, siblings, and other relatives are the closest people in our surroundings who care for us and live with us.
•   **Friends:** Friends are people of our age with whom we play, share, and learn, often living in our neighbourhood or going to the same school.
•   **Neighbours:** Neighbours are people who live near our house. We often interact with them and sometimes help each other.
•   **Teacher:** A teacher works at school and helps children learn new things, read, write, and understand the world.
•   **Doctor/Nurse:** Doctors and nurses work in hospitals or clinics and help us when we are sick or hurt, giving us medicine and care.
•   **Police Officer:** A police officer works at the police station and helps keep us safe, catches bad people, and helps maintain peace in the neighbourhood.
•   **Postman:** A postman delivers letters and parcels to our homes from the post office.
•   **Sweeper/Cleaner:** A sweeper or cleaner helps keep our streets, parks, and public places clean by collecting garbage.
•   **Shopkeeper:** A shopkeeper works in a shop and sells us things we need, like food, toys, and clothes.
•   **Farmer:** A farmer works in the fields to grow fruits, vegetables, and grains that we eat.
•   **Firefighter:** A firefighter works at the fire station and helps put out fires and rescue people from dangerous situations.
•   **Driver:** A driver drives vehicles like buses, cars, or trains, helping people travel from one place to another.
•   **Importance of Community Helpers:** All these people are very important because they provide essential services that make our lives easier, safer, and better.
•   **Respect and Gratitude:** We should always respect and be grateful to all the community helpers for their hard work and contributions to our surroundings.

•   **Keeping Our Surroundings Clean: Why and How:** This section emphasizes the importance of cleanliness in our environment and simple ways to achieve it.
•   **Importance of Cleanliness:** Keeping our surroundings clean is very important for our health, happiness, and the beauty of our environment.
•   **Health Benefits:** Clean surroundings prevent the spread of germs and diseases, helping us stay healthy and strong.
•   **Fresh Air:** Clean areas have fresh air, which is good for breathing and makes us feel energetic.
•   **Beautiful Environment:** A clean neighbourhood looks beautiful and is a pleasant place to live, play, and walk.
•   **Using Dustbins:** We should always throw garbage, waste papers, and food scraps into dustbins, never on the ground.
•   **Not Littering:** Littering means throwing waste carelessly on roads, parks, or public places, which makes our surroundings dirty. We must avoid it.
•   **Keeping Our Homes Clean:** We should help our parents keep our homes clean by putting our toys away, keeping our rooms tidy, and not scattering things.
•   **Keeping Our School Clean:** It is our responsibility to keep our school clean by not throwing waste in classrooms or playgrounds and using dustbins.
•   **Planting Trees:** Planting more trees and plants helps keep the air clean and makes our surroundings green and beautiful.
•   **Caring for Plants:** We should water plants regularly and not pluck their leaves or flowers unnecessarily.
•   **Role of Sweepers:** Sweepers and cleaners work hard to keep our public places clean, and we should support their efforts by not making their job harder.
•   **Waste Segregation (Basic):** Sometimes, we separate waste into different bins, like for dry waste (paper, plastic) and wet waste (food scraps), to help recycling.
•   **Personal Hygiene Connection:** Keeping our bodies clean (bathing, washing hands) is linked to keeping our surroundings clean, as both contribute to good health.
•   **Being a Responsible Citizen:** Keeping our surroundings clean is a duty of every person, making them a responsible member of the community.

•   **Safety in Our Surroundings:** This section teaches children basic safety rules to follow when they are in their surroundings, both inside and outside their homes.
•   **Traffic Rules (Basic):** When walking on roads, always look both ways (left, then right, then left again) before crossing to check for vehicles.
•   **Use Footpaths:** Always walk on the footpath or pavement, not in the middle of the road, to stay safe from traffic.
•   **Do Not Play on Roads:** Roads are for vehicles, not for playing. Playing on roads can be very dangerous.
•   **Stay with Adults:** Always stay close to your parents or a trusted adult when you are in crowded places like markets or parks.
•   **Do Not Talk to Strangers:** Never talk to or take anything from people you do not know, even if they seem friendly.
•   **Do Not Go with Strangers:** Never go anywhere with a stranger, even if they say your parents sent them. Always check with your parents first.
•   **Report to Adults:** If a stranger tries to talk to you or makes you feel uncomfortable, immediately tell your parents or a trusted adult.
•   **Play Safely in Parks:** Play on swings and slides carefully, wait for your turn, and do not push others.
•   **Do Not Touch Unknown Objects:** Never touch or pick up unknown objects, especially sharp or dangerous-looking ones, without an adult's permission.
•   **Basic Fire Safety:** Do not play with fire, matchsticks, or electrical switches. They can cause harm.
•   **Water Safety:** Never go near deep water bodies like ponds, rivers, or swimming pools alone. Always have an adult with you.
•   **Be Careful with Animals:** Do not tease or disturb stray animals. They might bite or scratch.
•   **Know Emergency Numbers (Simple):** Learn your parents' phone numbers or a simple emergency number like 100 (Police) or 101 (Fire) if taught by parents.
•   **Trust Your Feelings:** If a situation or a person makes you feel scared or uncomfortable, always listen to your feelings and tell an adult.

•   **Interacting with Surroundings: Review and Responsibility:** This final section summarizes how we engage with our surroundings and our role in maintaining them.
•   **Active Observation:** We interact with our surroundings by actively observing everything around us using our senses – seeing, hearing, smelling, and sometimes touching.
•   **Learning and Exploring:** Our surroundings provide endless opportunities for learning and exploration, from identifying different trees to understanding how a shop works.
•   **Playing and Recreation:** Parks, playgrounds, and open spaces in our surroundings offer places for us to play, exercise, and have fun.
•   **Respecting Living Things:** We must treat all living things in our surroundings, like plants and animals, with kindness and respect, not harming them.
